extracted.intended_audience: readers of fact checks, journalists, funders, policymakers and the general public interested in trustworthy information
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational standards and criteria Full Fact uses to produce, present and follow up on fact checks — covering accuracy, evidence, impartiality, transparency, use of expertise, tools and accountability. Intended to guide how fact checking work is evaluated and conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get their facts right
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone making serious claims in public debate—fact checkers included—should be prepared to get their facts right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact emphasises factual accuracy as the primary obligation. This underpins their mission to give people access to accurate information so they can make informed choices; fact checks focus on identifying, explaining and highlighting the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Back up what they say with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be supported by verifiable evidence; fact checks must link to sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact provides links to all sources so readers can check what has been said for themselves and draw their own conclusions. The organisation states repeatedly that they base outputs 'on verifiable facts' and that they 'provide links to all sources'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct their mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: When errors are found, they should be corrected publicly and promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact commits to correcting mistakes, follows up on fact checks by encouraging corrections or retractions, and has a 'Feedback & corrections' process. They also say they will call out those who fail to respond to requests to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on facts, not opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact checks should concentrate on verifiable factual claims rather than on expressing or adjudicating opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation explicitly states 'We focus on facts, not opinions.' This shapes selection and framing of work — choosing claims that can be verified or falsified rather than matters of taste or opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of claims to check
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority is given to claims made by politicians, public institutions, the media, and viral online content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact lists the types of claims it checks: those made by politicians, public institutions and the media, as well as viral content online. They also note a specific focus added on health misinformation (e.g., during Covid-19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality (fact-check claims, not people)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Fact does not take sides; they check claims rather than targeting people or parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states 'Full Fact doesn’t take sides. We fact check claims, not people.' Their board includes representatives of different viewpoints and they have 'rigorous safeguards in place to ensure our impartiality.' They caution that 'impartiality does not mean fake balance.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and fundraising neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain organisational independence from funders and ensure fundraising does not compromise neutrality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact is a registered charity and says 'we have fundraising guidelines in place to ensure neutrality' and that their independence is protected by support from thousands of people and organisations. Transparency about funding and adherence to guidelines are emphasised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about methods and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about how fact checks are done and provide source material so readers can assess the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact encourages readers to judge their individual fact checks and outputs as a whole. They 'provide links to all sources' and say 'it is for you to judge for yourself whether we succeed.' Transparency extends to giving access to evidence used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up and accountability after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively pursue accountability by asking for corrections/retractions and publicly follow up on responses (or lack thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact follows up on their fact checks by holding public figures and institutions accountable, encouraging corrections or retractions, and calling out those who fail to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate subject-matter expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring in qualified experts where specialised knowledge is required (e.g., clinical expertise for health claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact notes they added a specific focus on health misinformation during the Covid-19 pandemic and 'employ a qualified medical professional to add clinical expertise.' This demonstrates a standard to use relevant expertise for complex topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and use scalable, accurate tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in and deploy technology (including AI) that helps identify claims at scale while supporting reliable fact checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact describes building 'world-leading AI tools' that monitor millions of sentences daily and identify claims, matching them with prior fact checks when appropriate. The guidance implies tools should enable scale without sacrificing verifiability or accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate for systemic safeguards while protecting expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaign for stronger safeguards and laws against misinformation, balanced with protection for freedom of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact states they 'advocate for stronger safeguards against misinformation online, and campaign for better laws' and that they are 'determined to protect freedom of expression while also protecting people from harm,' indicating advocacy should balance safety and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop public critical thinking through training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide education and bespoke training to help people spot falsehoods and navigate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Fact 'focus[es] on critical thinking and provide[s] bespoke training' so that people can stay informed, spot falsehoods and navigate the digital world more confidently; training is presented as part of the evidence ecosystem.
